newsitem.title: INDIA: Nigeria, South Africa keen on Indian rice.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria, South Africa keen on Indian rice.

text.p: Export prices of Indian parboiled rice firmed marginally during the week as demand from Nigeria and South Africa picked up, traders said on Thursday.
"In the market there is a lot of demand for parboiled rice," said a leading New Delhi foodgrains exporter. "Main buyers are Nigeria and South Africa."
Traders said exporters in the past 10 days had signed export contracts for nearly 75,000 tonnes of parboiled rice.
They said five percent broken parboiled rice was quoted at $280 per tonne and 10 percent was traded $270-$273 per tonne FOB.
Traders said there was also good export demand for five percent broken rice from Commonweath of Independent States countries and for 100 percent broken rice from West Africa.
"Contracts for nearly 100,000 tonnes of exports of 100 percent broken rice were signed in the last 10 days," said Prem Garg, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter. "Shipments are going on."
Traders said five percent broken long grain non-Basmati rice was quoted at $305-310 per tonne FOB, 10 percent at $290, 15 percent at $275 and 25 percent at $260-265 per tonne.
"Contracts for about 20,000 tonnes of 100 percent rice was finalised with Senegal for July shipments," said an official in another New Delhi foodgrrains export firm.
The official said there was constant export enquiry about 100 percent broken and parboiled rice from African countries.
"Hopefully we will finalise some contracts this week," the official said.

Traders said sowing operations in most rice producing states had started as monsoon rains in these regions were good. "Next crop expectation is very good as the weather forecast until now is satisfactory," Garg said.
The Indian government on Wednesday forecast 1996/97 (July-June) rice output at 80.54 million tonnes, up from 79.62 million in the previous crop year.
